item.title: [LU-20869] reduce run time of long-running tests
item.description:
Timing data (Maloo finished sessions, 2026-09-03 to 2026-10-02) shows CI test time is spread thin: the 50 tests with the largest total time (runs x mean) are 22% of all test time outside the scale, performance, racer, sanity-benchmark and node-provisioning suites. No single test is more than 2%, so this is a series of small fixes aimed at tests that are slow because of how they are written.

Top 50 tests by total test-hours (runs x mean), 2026-09-03 to 2026-10-02. Mean in minutes, total in hours, share and cumulative are of the non-excluded pool (213,538 test-hours). The 50 tests total 47,115 hours, 22.1% of the pool.

Notes

  • 3 lustre-initialization (Deferred): an Autotest setup step, not in lustre-release; it needs a different fix.
  • 6 lnet-selftest test_smoke (Deferred): the batch needs about 500 s but SLOW=no caps the run at 300 s, so an early exit saves nothing; a real saving means less coverage. It also fails often (LU-16880, LU-16876).
  • 7 sanity-dom test_cleanup (Deferred): a cleanup step, not a test body; not yet reviewed.
  • 10 sanity test_900 (No change): the full unmount and remount is the test; the 20 s fail_loc pause is a small part of the time.
  • 13 sanity-sec test_31 (Deferred): reconfigures the LNet NIDs on every node and restarts the servers, so most of the time is mount cycles that the test needs; no obvious loop to remove. Revisit if a measurement shows otherwise.
  • 14 sanity test_123h (No change): 10001 file creates with touch and the statahead scan; the time is file-system speed, not a loop that grows, and createmany cannot make its zero-padded names. One baseline run failed with an I/O error (not investigated).
  • 16, 20 sanity test_133g and test_133f (Patch): both ended with a full cleanup and setup remount (60 to 150 s) after writing junk to proc files, which resets tunables the tests damage; the remount cannot simply be dropped, so 133g was folded into 133f and one remount follows both. 133g failed in 9 of about 78,000 suite runs in 90 days; its Maloo history ends. A standalone ONLY=133f now also runs the server part.
  • 17 sanity test_154g (Patch): the cost was llapi_fid_test test20, which builds 2000+ nested directories and calls fid2path on every level.
  • 24 sanity test_123f (No change): examined with the 123 series; nothing worth changing.
  • Rows marked "Not reviewed" have not been looked at yet.

comments.comment:
Exclusions: the timing pool leaves out the scale, performance, racer, sanity-benchmark and node-provisioning suites. The scale, performance and racer suites are long by design or measure throughput, and sanity-benchmark is a benchmark. node-provisioning is infrastructure setup rather than a test. Everything else is included, with no minimum run count, across 4,247 test rows.

Percentages in the table are of the 213,538 test-hours in the remaining suites. Counting the excluded suites too, the total is 237,004 test-hours and the top 50 are about 12.0% of that.

The table still contains two rows that are setup or cleanup steps rather than test bodies: lustre-initialization (an Autotest setup step, not in lustre-release) and sanity-dom test_cleanup. They are left in for now.

Patch uploaded: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/69388 (LU-20869 tests: merge sanity 133f and 133g). 133g's server badarea_io pass is folded into 133f so one cleanup/setup remount follows both client and server writes; 133g is removed. Local 3-node rocky9 cluster (separate client/MDS/OSS): before, 133f+133g = 57+58 s and 76+69 s (115 s, 145 s); after, merged 133f = 64 s, 64 s (80 s on a third run) with badarea_io confirmed on client, mds1 and ost1, and 133h/134a/134b passing after it. Saves 50-80 s locally. In CI (Rainshadow, 30 days) 133g averages 207 s over 14479 runs, so the expected saving is about 815 hours of test time per 30 days (133g's total of 834 h less a few seconds of server-part work added to 133f). 133g failed in 9 of about 78000 suite runs in 90 days (4 changes).

Uploaded https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/69389 (LU-20869 tests: speed up sanity 160n). Old loop did createmany + 10001 forked mrename + unlinkmany = 3 changelog records/file, 30000/pass, 3 passes (~90000 records) to pass the 65000 target. New: createmany/unlinkmany of 33000 files = 2 records/file, 66000 in one pass; fail_loc race part unchanged and verified to run and pass. ONLY=160n on a VM: before 757s and 1057s, after 43s and 27s. Rainshadow (30 days): 14503 runs, mean 276s. Expected CI saving roughly 14503 x ~250s = ~1000 hours per 30 days (CI hardware is faster than the VM, so estimate).

sanity test_255a: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/69390 (LU-20869 tests: shorten sanity 255a). The time is in ladvise_willread_performance(): 10 iterations x 3 passes, each reading every 4KiB block of a 100MB file at random (25600 sync reads, capped at 60s). CI mean 1028s over 14456 runs in 30 days (longest 2116s). Change: 3 iterations, an eighth of the blocks per pass; file size and thresholds unchanged. On a test VM cluster ONLY=255a: before 1089s, 2017s; after 170s, 166s, 137s, 252s. Expected saving about 800s per run, ~3200 runner-hours per 30 days (14456 runs); estimate, since VM disk speed varies a lot.

Cause: the loop-stop checks sat after a 'continue' taken when statahead timed 0s, so the loop ran on to 10000 files (~2 min of ls -l without statahead plus slow unlink) in some runs. Before: 123aa 35s and 300s; after: 60s and 85s (stops at 1000 files).
